---
name: oplm-mup-depth-sweep-hardening
description: Why/how the muP LR sweep was hardened for deep-model (800M) stability; residual-scaling analysis
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e1a20530-17fe-4111-afb5-8bed3fe3b55b
  modified: 2026-08-11T23:46:08.955Z
---

Redoing the muP LR sweep (`docs/LR_SWEEP.md`) because the original LR was
computed at 50M width-only with no depth adjustment; 170M/400M were fine but
800M (40 layers) was unstable from init and diverged before 5k steps.

Key architectural finding (non-obvious): production `norm_strategy=sandwich`
post-norms **both** sublayer outputs before the `alpha=1/√L` residual add, so
the `1/√(2L)` residual-writer init (`init_scale_output_projections`) is
renormalized away in the forward — the residual law is cleanly `1/√L` per write
and forward-stable at any depth. So the 800M blowup is a **training-dynamics**
failure (LR transfer / attention-logit / optimizer), not an init-time forward
explosion. Canon layers (A/B/C/D) are all sub-residuals *inside* sublayers on
normed streams — neutral to the 2L residual-write depth accounting.

Decision (July 2026): **keep residual α = 1/√L** (do not switch to CompleteP
1/L — it's a joint recipe and unlikely to be the fix). Harden instead:
- ~~widened `transfer` depth-LR exponent grid `0,0.25,0.5` → `0,0.5,0.75,1.0`~~
  **SUPERSEDED (Aug 2026): the exponent grid was removed entirely.** The
  exponent is derived, not free: with α=1/√L branch scaling, total one-step
  update ∝ η·L^(1/2−e), so e=0.5 exactly. (Calling e=1.0 "the CompleteP Adam
  value" was a category error — CompleteP's depth-flat LR pairs with its 1/L
  branch; grafting it onto 1/√L over-corrects.) `transfer` is now a fixed-width
  depth-ray *verification*: 170M width (768/12 heads), depths 12/24/48 via
  `model.num_hidden_layers` override, LR bracket ×{0.625,1,1.6} per finalist,
  `--exponent 0.5` pinned; selection = bracket center must win at every depth
  (else phase selects nothing; `winning_mults` in ranking shows drift
  direction). Cut ~1,950 node-hours (24 cells at 400M/800M/1B) to ~250 (18
  single-node cells) and removed the width/depth confound. Multi-preset array
  machinery in `_write_jobs`/`status` is now CLI-orphaned but kept + tested via
  `tests/sweep/conftest._generate_multi_preset_phase`;
- added `StabilityDiagnosticsCallback` (config flags `train.stability_diagnostics`,
  `train.stability_probe_every`) logging `diag/*`. **Hook-free** (user didn't want
  to disable `torch.compile`): grad norm every log (free, from
  `trainer._last_grad_norm`), plus a periodic *eager* diagnostic forward on the
  unwrapped model for per-depth residual RMS + logit RMS. No forward hooks →
  compile stays on. **Distributed-safety fix (after it hung an 8-GPU coarse run at
  the first probe with a 600s NCCL ALLREDUCE timeout):** the probe runs **main
  process only** and uses `output_hidden_states` on the tested SDPA path — NOT
  `output_attentions` (the memory-heavy manual-attention path, run on every rank,
  faulted async, escaped the sync-only try/except, and corrupted the next
  collective). Attention-entropy metric was dropped as part of this. `torch.cuda.
  synchronize()` inside the probe guard forces async faults to surface catchably.
  **After it crashed AGAIN, diagnostics were made fully opt-out**: the sweep
  phase commands take `--diagnostics/--no-diagnostics` (default OFF — the sweep
  ranks by val loss, so diagnostics are nice-to-have, not needed for selection);
  the flag pins `train.stability_diagnostics` per cell, overriding the base
  config. Probe batch shrunk to 1×128 as OOM insurance. Suspected remaining
  cause of the second crash: rank-0 OOM at production memory, or FSDP param
  all-gather on the single-rank probe forward (unconfirmed — no traceback);
- documented a long 800M stability probe (≥ failure horizon) and a 16-head
  (head_dim=80) control run to isolate the head-count-fix confounder;
- set proxy warmup to ~10% of each phase's horizon (was a flat 5,000 = 50% at
  the 10k `coarse`/`bridge`/`confirm`): coarse/bridge/confirm=1,000, refine=2,000,
  `transfer` per-preset `--warmup` list `1000,2000,1000`, `scale` stays 5,000 (~5%).
  Rationale: a 50% warmup fraction tolerates a hotter peak LR than production's
  ~0.4% warmup, biasing LR selection upward; warmup fraction doesn't transfer
  across horizon.

See [[oplm-plans-go-in-todos-md]], [[oplm-run-ci-gates-before-done]].

content.text:
Done — `transfer` is rewritten as a fixed-width depth-ray verification, all gates pass (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check` on `src/`, and 1,641 tests). Changes are uncommitted on `docs/mup-lr-sweep`. Answers to your two questions first:

## 1) Yes — all four completed phases are fully reusable

Two reasons, one practical and one structural:

- **Interface unchanged.** The new `transfer` still takes `--from $SWEEP/refine-replicate/phase.json` and consumes the same selected candidates (`lr`, `output_mult`) that replicate already produced. You just run the new command against your existing manifest.
- **Your proxy data is exponent-agnostic by construction.** Everything through replicate ran at 170M, which is L=24 — the μP reference depth, where the depth correction `(24/L)^e ≡ 1` for *any* exponent. Nothing about changing the depth-scaling policy retroactively invalidates those results; the finalists you already have are exactly the right input. (This is also why the rewrite requires depth 24 in the ray: that leg re-checks the finalist at its native geometry and anchors the bracket.)

## 2) No — keep sandwich norm and the gates; they're a stability asset, not a liability

They break the *derivability* of the depth exponent, not LR transfer itself, and the failure direction matters:

- **Sandwich norm caps the classic blow-up mode.** The post-norm bounds each branch contribution to `α·gate·Θ(1)` regardless of weight growth — it makes the response to a slightly-wrong exponent *flatter*, not sharper. You traded analytic cleanliness for dynamical robustness, which is the right trade for a production run. The gates are per-channel scalars behind a norm, on AdamW; their main risk is slow drift over long horizons, which is exactly what `diag/*` and the deep stability probe watch.
- **Removing them would invalidate your existing sweep data** — LR optima are architecture-specific, so you'd restart the funnel from smoke, forfeiting the reuse from question 1 *and* a measured ablation win, to buy a theoretical guarantee (CompleteP's) that itself assumes plain pre-LN blocks you wouldn't fully match anyway.
- **The correct hedge for reduced predictability is cheap empirical verification**, which is what the rewrite installs. Revisit only if the depth ray shows non-monotone or non-power-law drift — that would be direct evidence the gate/norm interaction matters.

## What the rewrite does

`oplm sweep transfer` no longer sweeps exponents at 400M/800M/1B. It now generates a **fixed-width depth ray**: every cell keeps 170M geometry (hidden 768, 12 heads) and overrides only `num_hidden_layers` over `--depths 12,24,48`, crossing each replicated finalist with an LR bracket `--lr-mults 0.625,1,1.6` on top of the pinned correction `--exponent 0.5` (the value derived from the frozen `1/√L` branch: total update ∝ `η·L^(1/2−e)`). That's 18 single-node cells (~250 node-hours, auto-submittable) instead of 24 multi-node cells (~1,950 node-hours), with 4× depth leverage instead of 2× and no width/heads/horizon confound.

Selection changed to match: a finalist **transfers** when the bracket center wins at every depth (missing/non-finite center disqualifies; a diverged *edge* merely loses). Transferring candidates rank by mean center loss; the winner proceeds to `bridge` carrying `depth_exponent=0.5`. If nobody transfers, the phase selects nothing and each ranking entry's new `winning_mults` field shows the per-depth drift direction — hot at depth 48 means the correction is too strong, cold means too weak, and the drift slope is itself the measured exponent.

Docs: `LR_SWEEP.md`'s exponent section is replaced with the derivation and the corrected CompleteP framing (e=1.0 is *not* "the CompleteP value" under a `1/√L` branch — CompleteP's depth-flat LR pairs with its `1/L` branch), the funnel/node/cost tables are updated (transfer moved to the auto-submit group, with a note on depth-48 memory headroom), and `MUP.md` no longer describes the exponent as empirically grid-selected. The deep-stability-probe section now explicitly owns the production-geometry coverage that transfer gave up. Tests were restructured accordingly — the multi-preset Slurm-array/status machinery transfer used to exercise is now covered by a dedicated `_generate_multi_preset_phase` helper, and new tests cover the bracket generation, the layers override landing in `run.yaml`, and both ranking edge cases.

One operational note: since the LR grid is 1.6×-spaced, one finalist's ×1.6 cell can land on another finalist's ×1 LR — run IDs now embed the depth and multiplier (`transfer-170M-d48-lr0.004-om1-a0.5-x1.6-s42`) so W&B names stay unambiguous.

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from oplm.slurm.config import BatchPlan, PhaseTable, SlurmConfig, resolve_batch_plan

RAW = {
    "partition": "hpc-mid",
    "time_limit": {"default": "168:00:00", "analyze": "01:00:00"},
    "cpus_per_task": 128,
    "gpus_per_node": 8,
    "exclusive": True,
    "mem": "0",
    "log_dir": "/mnt/home/briney/logs",
    "env_file": "/mnt/home/briney/.env",
    "container_image": "/mnt/data/containers/dl.sqsh",
    "container_mounts": ["/mnt/data:/mnt/data", "/tmp:/tmp"],
    "install": "pip install oplm[train]",
    "max_concurrent": 4,
    "nodes": {
        "default": {"170M": 1, "400M": 4, "800M": 8, "1B": 8},
        "bridge": {"170M": 4},
        "confirm": {"800M": 8},
    },
    "max_batch_size": {"170M": 256, "400M": 256, "800M": 256, "1B": 128},
}


def test_scalar_table_applies_everywhere() -> None:
    table = PhaseTable.from_value(4, name="nodes")
    assert table.resolve(phase=None, preset=None) == 4
    assert table.resolve(phase="bridge", preset="800M") == 4


def test_preset_table_without_default_key() -> None:
    table = PhaseTable.from_value({"170M": 1, "400M": 4}, name="nodes")
    assert table.resolve(phase=None, preset="400M") == 4
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="800M"):
        table.resolve(phase=None, preset="800M")


def test_phase_override_beats_default() -> None:
    cfg = SlurmConfig.from_mapping(RAW)
    assert cfg.nodes.resolve(phase="coarse", preset="170M") == 1
    assert cfg.nodes.resolve(phase="bridge", preset="170M") == 4
    assert cfg.nodes.resolve(phase="confirm", preset="800M") == 8
    # A phase override that omits a preset falls back to default for that preset.
    assert cfg.nodes.resolve(phase="bridge", preset="400M") == 4


def test_time_limit_resolves_per_phase() -> None:
    """`time_limit` entries are bare values, not preset maps: they apply to every preset."""
    cfg = SlurmConfig.from_mapping(RAW)
    assert cfg.time_limit.resolve(phase="coarse", preset="170M") == "168:00:00"
    assert cfg.time_limit.resolve(phase="analyze", preset=None) == "01:00:00"
    # A phase with no override falls back to default regardless of preset.
    assert cfg.time_limit.resolve(phase="transfer", preset="1B") == "168:00:00"


def test_exact_preset_beats_wildcard() -> None:
    table = PhaseTable.from_value({"default": 1, "bridge": {"170M": 4}}, name="nodes")
    assert table.resolve(phase="bridge", preset="170M") == 4
    # bridge has no 800M entry and no wildcard, so default's wildcard applies.
    assert table.resolve(phase="bridge", preset="800M") == 1
    assert table.resolve(phase="coarse", preset="170M") == 1


def test_phase_wildcard_beats_default_exact_preset() -> None:
    """A phase's own wildcard must win over `default`'s exact-preset entry.

    This pins the priority ordering: `resolve` must exhaust the phase's own table (exact, then
    wildcard) before ever consulting `default`. A regression that instead checked exact-preset
    matches across both tables before falling back to wildcards would return `default`'s `1`
    here instead of `coarse`'s wildcard `8`.
    """
    table = PhaseTable.from_value({"default": {"170M": 1}, "coarse": 8}, name="nodes")
    assert table.resolve(phase="coarse", preset="170M") == 8


def test_missing_required_field_raises() -> None:
    raw = {key: value for key, value in RAW.items() if key != "partition"}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="partition"):
        SlurmConfig.from_mapping(raw)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["gpus_per_node", "cpus_per_task", "max_concurrent"])
def test_non_positive_ints_rejected(field: str) -> None:
    raw = {**RAW, field: 0}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=field):
        SlurmConfig.from_mapping(raw)


def test_non_positive_max_batch_size_rejected() -> None:
    raw = {**RAW, "max_batch_size": {"170M": 0}}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_batch_size"):
        SlurmConfig.from_mapping(raw)


def test_bool_max_batch_size_rejected() -> None:
    """`bool` is an `int` subclass; a bare `int(value)` coercion would silently accept it."""
    raw = {**RAW, "max_batch_size": {"170M": True}}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"max_batch_size\['170M'\].*True"):
        SlurmConfig.from_mapping(raw)


def test_non_numeric_max_batch_size_rejected() -> None:
    """A non-numeric value must raise this module's actionable message, not a raw int() error."""
    raw = {**RAW, "max_batch_size": {"170M": "oops"}}
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"max_batch_size\['170M'\].*oops"):
        SlurmConfig.from_mapping(raw)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("global_examples", "nodes", "cap", "expected"),
    [
        # The spec's node table: every row resolves to accum == 1.
        (
            2048,
            1,
            256,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=256, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=8),
        ),
        (
            2048,
            4,
            256,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=64, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=32),
        ),
        (
            2048,
            8,
            256,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=32, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=64),
        ),
        (
            2048,
            8,
            128,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=32, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=64),
        ),
        (
            8192,
            4,
            256,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=256, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=32),
        ),
        (
            8192,
            8,
            256,
            BatchPlan(per_device_batch=128, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=64),
        ),
    ],
)
def test_batch_plan_matches_the_spec_table(
    global_examples: int, nodes: int, cap: int, expected: BatchPlan
) -> None:
    assert (
        resolve_batch_plan(
            global_examples=global_examples, world_size=nodes * 8, max_batch_size=cap
        )
        == expected
    )


def test_cap_forces_accumulation() -> None:
    # 2048 / 8 = 256 per device at accum 1, over a cap of 128, so accum must rise to 2.
    plan = resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=2048, world_size=8, max_batch_size=128)
    assert plan == BatchPlan(per_device_batch=128, gradient_accumulation_steps=2, world_size=8)


def test_local_world_size_still_lands_on_the_global_batch() -> None:
    """--local passes its actual process count, so a 400M cell keeps a 2048 global batch."""
    plan = resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=2048, world_size=8, max_batch_size=256)
    assert plan.per_device_batch * plan.gradient_accumulation_steps * plan.world_size == 2048


def test_indivisible_global_batch_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not divisible"):
        resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=2048, world_size=24, max_batch_size=256)


def test_global_batch_smaller_than_world_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not divisible"):
        resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=4, world_size=8, max_batch_size=256)


def test_prime_base_forces_search_past_non_divisor_candidates() -> None:
    """970 / 10 = 97 (prime): only accum in {1, 97} divides it evenly.

    A ceil-based implementation (``accum = ceil(base / cap)``, ``per_device = ceil(base /
    accum)``, with no check that ``accum`` actually divides ``base``) would compute
    ``accum = ceil(97 / 32) = 4`` and ``per_device = ceil(97 / 4) = 25``, giving a product of
    ``25 * 4 * 10 = 1000 != 970`` -- silently violating the exact-global-batch invariant that
    makes sweep cells comparable. The real search must reject accum=2..96 (every one a
    non-divisor of 97) before landing on accum=97, per_device=1.
    """
    plan = resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=970, world_size=10, max_batch_size=32)
    assert plan == BatchPlan(per_device_batch=1, gradient_accumulation_steps=97, world_size=10)
    assert plan.per_device_batch * plan.gradient_accumulation_steps * plan.world_size == 970


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", ["global_examples", "world_size", "max_batch_size"])
def test_resolve_batch_plan_rejects_bool(field: str) -> None:
    """`bool` is an `int` subclass; a bare range check would silently accept it and store it.

    Confirmed as a real leak (not just a theoretical one): before this fix,
    ``resolve_batch_plan(global_examples=8, world_size=True, max_batch_size=8)`` returned
    ``BatchPlan(per_device_batch=8, gradient_accumulation_steps=1, world_size=True)`` -- a
    `bool` stored in an `int` field, ready to propagate into anything rendered downstream.
    """
    kwargs: dict[str, int] = {"global_examples": 2048, "world_size": 8, "max_batch_size": 256}
    kwargs[field] = True
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=field):
        resolve_batch_plan(**kwargs)

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from typer.testing import CliRunner

from oplm.sweep import phases
from oplm.sweep.common import load_phase
from tests.slurm.test_submit import _install_stub
from tests.sweep.conftest import _write_base_config

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path

    import pytest

runner = CliRunner()


def test_single_preset_phase_emits_one_array(coarse_phase: Path) -> None:
    jobs = coarse_phase.parent / "jobs"
    assert (jobs / "170M.sbatch").exists()
    assert (jobs / "170M.jobs").exists()
    assert (jobs / "analyze.sbatch").exists()
    assert (jobs / "submit.sh").exists()
    cells = (jobs / "170M.jobs").read_text().splitlines()
    assert len(cells) == 7
    assert "#SBATCH --array=0-6%4" in (jobs / "170M.sbatch").read_text()


def test_multi_preset_phase_emits_one_array_per_preset(multi_preset_phase: Path) -> None:
    """Slurm arrays need homogeneous resources, and node count varies by preset."""
    jobs = multi_preset_phase.parent / "jobs"
    for preset, nodes in (("400M", 4), ("800M", 8), ("1B", 8)):
        text = (jobs / f"{preset}.sbatch").read_text()
        assert f"#SBATCH --nodes={nodes}" in text
    submit = (jobs / "submit.sh").read_text()
    assert "--dependency=afterany:$A_400M:$A_800M:$A_1B" in submit


def test_transfer_emits_single_170m_array_across_depths(transfer_phase: Path) -> None:
    """The depth ray keeps every cell on the 170M single-node allocation: one array total."""
    jobs = transfer_phase.parent / "jobs"
    text = (jobs / "170M.sbatch").read_text()
    assert "#SBATCH --nodes=1" in text
    assert "#SBATCH --array=0-8%4" in text
    ids = (jobs / "170M.jobs").read_text().split()
    assert len(ids) == 9  # 1 candidate x 3 depths x 3 bracket multipliers
    assert {run_id.split("-")[1] for run_id in ids} == {"d12", "d24", "d48"}


def test_analyze_job_is_cpu_only(coarse_phase: Path) -> None:
    text = (coarse_phase.parent / "jobs" / "analyze.sbatch").read_text()
    assert "--gres" not in text
    assert "oplm sweep analyze" in text
    assert "#SBATCH --time=01:00:00" in text


def test_cells_file_order_matches_manifest(coarse_phase: Path) -> None:
    manifest = json.loads(coarse_phase.read_text())
    cells = (coarse_phase.parent / "jobs" / "170M.jobs").read_text().split()
    assert cells == [run["id"] for run in manifest["runs"]]


def test_manifest_records_provenance(coarse_phase: Path) -> None:
    from importlib.metadata import version

    manifest = json.loads(coarse_phase.read_text())
    assert manifest["oplm_version"] == version("oplm")
    assert manifest["generated_at"]


def test_generated_scripts_are_valid_bash(coarse_phase: Path) -> None:
    for script in sorted((coarse_phase.parent / "jobs").glob("*.sbatch")):
        subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", str(script)], check=True)
    subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", str(coarse_phase.parent / "jobs" / "submit.sh")], check=True)


def test_confirm_phase_emits_its_single_array(confirm_phase: Path) -> None:
    """`confirm_phase` (800M, one candidate) exercises the single-preset path a second way."""
    jobs = confirm_phase.parent / "jobs"
    text = (jobs / "800M.sbatch").read_text()
    assert "#SBATCH --nodes=8" in text
    assert "#SBATCH --array=0-0%4" in text


def test_submit_flag_submits_all_and_records_job_ids(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """`--submit` submits every entry via the fake `sbatch` on PATH and records the ids."""
    log = tmp_path / "sbatch.log"
    _install_stub(
        tmp_path,
        monkeypatch,
        "sbatch",
        f'#!/bin/bash\necho "$@" >> "{log}"\ncount=$(wc -l < "{log}")\necho $((900000 + count))\n',
    )
    config = _write_base_config(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "coarse"
    result = runner.invoke(
        phases.app,
        ["coarse", "--config", str(config), "--out", str(out), "--submit"],
    )
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    manifest = load_phase(out / "phase.json")
    assert manifest.job_ids is not None
    assert set(manifest.job_ids) == {"A_170M", "ANALYZE"}
    assert log.exists()


def test_local_and_submit_are_mutually_exclusive(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = _write_base_config(tmp_path)
    result = runner.invoke(
        phases.app,
        [
            "coarse",
            "--config",
            str(config),
            "--out",
            str(tmp_path / "coarse"),
            "--local",
            "--submit",
        ],
    )
    assert result.exit_code != 0
    assert "mutually exclusive" in result.output


def test_scale_command_has_no_submit_flag(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """`scale` generates only -- it has no `--submit` (or `--local`) flag at all."""
    result = runner.invoke(phases.app, ["scale", "--help"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "--submit" not in result.output
    assert "--local" not in result.output

---
name: oplm-mup-depth-sweep-hardening
description: Why/how the muP LR sweep was hardened for deep-model (800M) stability; residual-scaling analysis
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e1a20530-17fe-4111-afb5-8bed3fe3b55b
  modified: 2026-08-11T23:46:23.701Z
---

Redoing the muP LR sweep (`docs/LR_SWEEP.md`) because the original LR was
computed at 50M width-only with no depth adjustment; 170M/400M were fine but
800M (40 layers) was unstable from init and diverged before 5k steps.

Key architectural finding (non-obvious): production `norm_strategy=sandwich`
post-norms **both** sublayer outputs before the `alpha=1/√L` residual add, so
the `1/√(2L)` residual-writer init (`init_scale_output_projections`) is
renormalized away in the forward — the residual law is cleanly `1/√L` per write
and forward-stable at any depth. So the 800M blowup is a **training-dynamics**
failure (LR transfer / attention-logit / optimizer), not an init-time forward
explosion. Canon layers (A/B/C/D) are all sub-residuals *inside* sublayers on
normed streams — neutral to the 2L residual-write depth accounting.

Decision (July 2026): **keep residual α = 1/√L** (do not switch to CompleteP
1/L — it's a joint recipe and unlikely to be the fix). Harden instead:
- ~~widened `transfer` depth-LR exponent grid `0,0.25,0.5` → `0,0.5,0.75,1.0`~~
  **SUPERSEDED (Aug 2026): the exponent grid was removed entirely.** The
  exponent is derived, not free: with α=1/√L branch scaling, total one-step
  update ∝ η·L^(1/2−e), so e=0.5 exactly. (Calling e=1.0 "the CompleteP Adam
  value" was a category error — CompleteP's depth-flat LR pairs with its 1/L
  branch; grafting it onto 1/√L over-corrects.) `transfer` is now a fixed-width
  depth-ray *verification*: 170M width (768/12 heads), depths 12/24/48 via
  `model.num_hidden_layers` override, LR bracket ×{0.625,1,1.6} per finalist,
  `--exponent 0.5` pinned; selection = bracket center must win at every depth
  (else phase selects nothing; `winning_mults` in ranking shows drift
  direction). Cut ~1,950 node-hours (24 cells at 400M/800M/1B) to ~250 (18
  single-node cells) and removed the width/depth confound. Multi-preset array
  machinery in `_write_jobs`/`status` is now CLI-orphaned but kept + tested via
  `tests/sweep/conftest._generate_multi_preset_phase`;
- added `StabilityDiagnosticsCallback` (config flags `train.stability_diagnostics`,
  `train.stability_probe_every`) logging `diag/*`. **Hook-free** (user didn't want
  to disable `torch.compile`): grad norm every log (free, from
  `trainer._last_grad_norm`), plus a periodic *eager* diagnostic forward on the
  unwrapped model for per-depth residual RMS + logit RMS. No forward hooks →
  compile stays on. **Distributed-safety fix (after it hung an 8-GPU coarse run at
  the first probe with a 600s NCCL ALLREDUCE timeout):** the probe runs **main
  process only** and uses `output_hidden_states` on the tested SDPA path — NOT
  `output_attentions` (the memory-heavy manual-attention path, run on every rank,
  faulted async, escaped the sync-only try/except, and corrupted the next
  collective). Attention-entropy metric was dropped as part of this. `torch.cuda.
  synchronize()` inside the probe guard forces async faults to surface catchably.
  **After it crashed AGAIN, diagnostics were made fully opt-out**: the sweep
  phase commands take `--diagnostics/--no-diagnostics` (default OFF — the sweep
  ranks by val loss, so diagnostics are nice-to-have, not needed for selection);
  the flag pins `train.stability_diagnostics` per cell, overriding the base
  config. Probe batch shrunk to 1×128 as OOM insurance. Suspected remaining
  cause of the second crash: rank-0 OOM at production memory, or FSDP param
  all-gather on the single-rank probe forward (unconfirmed — no traceback);
- documented a long 800M stability probe (≥ failure horizon) and a 16-head
  (head_dim=80) control run to isolate the head-count-fix confounder;
- set proxy warmup to ~10% of each phase's horizon (was a flat 5,000 = 50% at
  the 10k `coarse`/`bridge`/`confirm`): coarse/bridge/confirm=1,000, refine=2,000,
  `transfer` scalar `--steps 10000 --warmup 1000` (uniform across depths since the
  Aug 2026 depth-ray rewrite), `scale` stays 5,000 (~5%).
  Rationale: a 50% warmup fraction tolerates a hotter peak LR than production's
  ~0.4% warmup, biasing LR selection upward; warmup fraction doesn't transfer
  across horizon.

See [[oplm-plans-go-in-todos-md]], [[oplm-run-ci-gates-before-done]].

Done — every `transfer` depth-ray cell now distributes across 4 nodes (32 GPUs, data parallel, 64 examples per device, `gradient_accumulation_steps=1`). All 1,641 tests pass, and `ruff`/`ty` are clean on the changed scope.

Node counts are resolved from the config's `nodes` table rather than hardcoded, so the change is one table entry plus its reflections:

- **`docs/LR_SWEEP.md`** — the production config's `slurm.nodes` block gains `transfer: {170M: 4}` (matching `bridge`/`replicate`), the node table now shows 4 nodes / 64 per device with wall times dropping to ~1.5/3/6 h for depths 12/24/48, and the depth-48 memory caveat is gone — at 64 per device there's ample headroom, so the old "add a 2-node override if it OOMs" note no longer applies. The cost-split note now flags that `transfer` also needs a 4-node allocation before you `--submit`.
- **`tests/slurm/test_config.py`** — the shared `RAW` slurm fixture (which the sweep test configs mirror from) gains the same `transfer: {170M: 4}` entry.
- **Tests** — the jobs test asserts `--nodes=4` for the single 170M array, and the generation test now pins the resolved batch plan: every cell must record `(nodes, per_device_batch, gradient_accumulation_steps) == (4, 64, 1)`, so a regression in the plan derivation can't slip through.

One thing worth knowing: total compute is unchanged (~250 node-hours) — the 4-node spread buys wall time, taking the whole 18-cell phase from ~2 days to well under one with `max_concurrent: 4`. The phase remains in the auto-`--submit` group.
